# Fireworks raises GPU rates up to 30%

09/01/26, 03:35 AM

 Follows up on Owning a Model Costs $124K per Benchmark Point 

Earlier analysis of Fireworks’ Training API argued that a narrow team should train its own model only when specialization pays back roughly $124,000 per benchmark point plus engineering cost. Fireworks’ current on-demand price table raises H100/H200 from $7 to $8 per GPU-hour, B200 from $10 to $13, B300 from $12 to $15, and GB300 from $18 to $20 starting September 1—an 11%–30% increase. The call holds: dedicated reinforcement training still belongs to a narrow buyer set, but new runs should use the higher rates because Fireworks prices reinforcement fine-tuning by GPU-hour.

results.title: Best AI Inference Orchestration Platforms 2026 | Omid Saffari
results.author: Omid Saffari
highlights:
The cleanest common baseline available across four vendors is one continuously used H100 for 730 hours. The rates below were live on September 1, 2026. They are deliberately not presented as an apples-to-apples performance comparison: H100 variants, regions, software stacks, support, and service behavior differ.

| Platform | Public H100 rate | 730-hour baseline | 10% of four-GPU fleet |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Modal | $3.9492/hour, normalized from $0.001097/second | $2,882.92 | $1,153.17 |
| Together AI | $3.99/GPU-hour, current promotion | $2,912.70 | $1,165.08 |
| Baseten | $6.4998/hour, normalized from $0.10833/minute | $4,744.85 | $1,897.94 |
| Fireworks AI | $8/GPU-hour from September 1 | $5,840 | $2,336 |

...

The table is a budget baseline, not a benchmark. Modal Team would turn its $2,882.92 compute line into **$ 3,032.92** after adding the $250 plan and subtracting its $100 monthly credit. Together AI's displayed regular $5.49 H100 rate would make the same month **$ 4,007.70**, a $1,095 increase when the $3.99 promotion ends if no new deal replaces it. Fireworks AI's H100 rate rose from $7 through August 31 to $8 from September 1, adding **$ 730** to a 730-hour month.

...

The price difference is model-specific. Fireworks' live serverless page lists GLM-5.3 Standard at $1.40 input, $0.26 cached input, and $4.40 output per million tokens. Priority raises those figures to $1.75, $0.325, and $5.50. GLM-5.2 Fast is $2.10 input, $0.21 cached input, and $6.60 output. Batch inference is billed at 50% of serverless input and output prices, which can be the decisive saving for overnight classification, enrichment, or evaluation work that does not need an immediate response.

Dedicated capacity changed price on the day of this verification. The live Fireworks pricing page lists H100 and H200 at $8 per GPU-hour, B200 at $13, B300 at $15, and GB300 at $20 from September 1. H100 had been $7 through August 31, so one continuously used H100 now adds $730 to a 730-hour month. Region-restricted deployments carry a 1.5x premium, turning that H100 into $12 per hour and $8,760 for the normalized month.

Fireworks earns its place when the application can exploit different lanes. A B2B product could keep normal requests on Standard, route a narrow paid workflow to Priority, push interactive work to Fast when supported, and move asynchronous evaluation to batch. It loses when the buyer needs one custom deployment with hybrid portability, or when region restrictions turn a competitive base rate into a premium one.

Best for: A product team serving open models that can route interactive, peak-reliability, and asynchronous work to different price lanes.
Standout: Standard, Priority, Fast, and half-price batch paths under one managed provider.
Pricing: Per-model serverless; $1 starting credit; on-demand H100 and H200 at $8/GPU-hour from September 1; other current GPU rates listed above.
Free trial: $1 in free credits.

## Hidden Costs Developers Miss

1. Model catalog churn — Llama 3 8B "standard" and Mixtral 8x7B/8x22B are no longer named line items on Together AI's pricing page; anyone budgeting off an older article citing those exact SKUs needs to remap to current equivalents.
2. Fireworks' Sep 1, 2026 GPU price step-up — on-demand H100 rose from $7.00 to $8.00/hour, and B200 from $10.00 to $13.00/hour, already in effect as of this writing.
3. Together's dedicated H100 promo expiry — the $3.99/hour rate is explicitly marked as valid only until 09/30/26; the list price reverts to $5.49/hour afterward.
4. Cached-input asymmetry — Fireworks discounts cached input by ~97% ($0.22 → $0.007) versus Together's ~79% ($0.14 → $0.03) for this model; the platform that looks cheaper can flip for cache-heavy workloads at some volumes even though it doesn't at the scale modeled below.
5. Fireworks region-restricted premium — dedicated deployments locked to a specific region carry a stated 1.5x price premium.
6. Fireworks US-only serverless premium — as of September 1, 2026, US-only-routed serverless models are priced 50% above the global rate.
7. Fine-tuning minimums — Together AI's standard fine-tuning jobs carry a $4.00 minimum charge per job regardless of dataset size; per-model minimums for larger models run higher.

# Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50

Nebius lists higher on demand GPU prices effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU hour. H200 rises from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50. This round is 17% to 21%. It is reported to be the second increase since May. [1] [2]

Published September 28, 2026 Announced, effective October 1, 2026

## Disclosed terms

HGX H100, per GPU hour

$3.85 now, $4.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX H200, per GPU hour

$4.50 now, $5.40 from October 1 [1]

HGX B200, per GPU hour

$7.15 now, $8.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX B300, per GPU hour

$7.85 now, $9.50 from October 1 [1]

...

### What changed

Nebius's pricing page now shows two on demand columns: today's rate and a rate effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises 17%, H200 20%, B200 19% and B300 21%. [1]

Spot rates still start at $0.79 for H100 and H200 and $0.99 for B200 and B300. RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80. CPU only instances also rise. Nebius still advertises commitment discounts of up to 35% off on demand for multi month cluster reservations. [1]

Nebius's pricing page does not give a reason for the change.

...

H200: At $5.40, Nebius moves above Runpod ($4.59) and Verda ($4.55).

...

B200: At $8.50, Nebius moves well above Lambda ($6.69) and Runpod ($6.79). CoreWeave's 8 GPU instance works out to about $8.60 per GPU.

B300: At $9.50, Nebius moves above Verda ($8.20) and Scaleway ($7.50). Together AI lists $9.99.

Configurations differ. vCPUs, memory, storage, networking and minimum allocation all vary. A lower hourly rate is not a lower project cost on its own.

...

If you run on Nebius on demand today, your bill goes up October 1 unless your contract says otherwise. Check whether your agreement fixes the rate.

If you have a Nebius quote in hand, ask which rate it uses.
